To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in rodents neurofilaments are present in the axon terminal plexus of B-type horizontal cells and not in the axonless cell bodies of A-type cells, while in the guinea pig they are present in both types of horizontal cell.
neurofilament immunostainings of rodent retinal horizontal cell plexuses show the axon terminal networks of the axonbearing B-type horizontal cells.
the axon-bearing horizontal B-type cells contain neurofilament proteins, and that the axonal systems of B-type cells are present in the guinea pig, but are missing in rat and gerbill retina.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unexpected presence of neurofilament immunoreactivity in axon-bearing B- and A-type horizontal cells of the rodent retina.
the unexpected presence of neurofilament proteins in the axon terminal system of the axon bearing horizontal cells in the retina.

the distribution of neurofilaments and the presence of A-type horizontal cells, and it is shown that the neurofilament immunoreactive plexus in the mammalian retina is formed by B-type axon terminals, and that the A-type horizontal cell does not exist in the rodent retina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of neurofilament protein in horizontal cell axon terminals is a general mammalian feature.
the presence of neurofilament immunoreactivity does not necessarily imply the presence of axon-bearing horizontal cell types.

neurofilaments are present in axon-bearing B- type horizontal cells of all mammalian species studied so far, and that neurofilaments may be present in the axonless, A-type horizontal cell of some mammals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in all mammalian retinas studied so far, neurofilament expression in the horizontal cell system is restricted to B-type axon-bearing horizontal cell terminals.
the presence of neurofilament immunostains in the horizontal cell plexuses in the rodent retina is due to the presence of B-type axon terminals.

in all mammalian species investigated to date neurofilament immunostainings of the retinas have shown the presence of neurofilament-containing horizontal cell plexuses, which in some cases were interpreted as A-type cell plexuses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are neurofilaments in B-type horizontal cells and that neurofilaments are not a marker for A-type cells in the retina.
neurofilament immunostainings are not a reliable marker for horizontal cell types.
neurofilaments are not restricted to axons of the mammalian visual system but are present in axons and axon terminal systems in both A-type and B-type horizontal cell subtypes.
